title: Level 3 stores the references only the toolchain sees, and a roster of the targets it defines
objective: Level 3 also keeps the references only the language's toolchain sees, for definitions inside the project: uses of the project's own fields, consts and statics, its types and variants in patterns, and its functions passed as values, so that `intent search --target` answers who uses one of them exactly and a never-referenced answer is exact for those kinds; and it keeps a roster of the targets the toolchain defines, so `--target` tells a target nothing references from a misspelt one.
context:
Ruled by hv on 2026-09-17 ("Ok, A now, then B post."; hv decision 22 on hv's board) after ST0076 landed level 3 under rule A: a resolved row always joins a written reference (same file, line and name), and a reference only the toolchain sees is counted and not stored (vc decision 25 (2), the level-3 core's module doc). This thread is B, for the line after the close-out.

Measured on the Intent repository by vc on 2026-09-17, on the live `intent index resolve --lang rust` run (ea81a6c58, store schema 29) and recounted independently from the export and the store to the unit: rust-analyzer reports 242,375 references; 133,788 are stored under rule A; 74,354 are dropped by design (57,482 locals, 16,845 operator references, 27 multi-line); 34,233 are real references the syntax index never wrote, counted as unmatched and not stored. Of those, 12,859 are uses of the project's own fields, consts and statics; 6,051 are mentions of its own modules (`mod x;` lines and path heads); 1,484 are its own types and variants where the syntax queries do not look, mostly patterns; 190 are its own functions passed as values, plus 2 macros; and 13,647 point outside the project (`std` path segments, `#[test]` and derive names, `Ok`, `Err`, `Some` and `None`), which nobody asks about. So the population this thread stores is about 20,600 rows here, some 16% more than rule A stores, and it is Rust-only in effect: the Elixir tracer reports no field access.

What it needs, as vc sized it (M to L): one predicate at write in the level-3 core (`intentsvcs::index::resolved::join`), which today drops a reference that joins no written row; a hit shape in the search surfaces for a reference that has no syntax row (a level-3-only reference carries its path, line and name from the toolchain and no `symbols` row); a table of the targets the toolchain defines, one schema rung, filled by the Rust reader from the export's definition occurrences and by the Elixir reader from the definition rows it prints; `--target` on a defined target no row references answering "defined at path:line, referenced by nothing" instead of the note that a target nothing references and a misspelt one read the same; `intent index status` counting stored-unwritten rows apart from the external unmatched; and arms for each. The side table has no foreign key to the written rows, so nothing landed under rule A is undone.

## Elixir, measured on Laksa

Measured by dc on 2026-09-17 on a scratch copy of Laksa, with a worktree binary built from ST0076 WP-06's bank `c4b326db`. The first run was forced and took 13.6 s. It matched 30,856 references, left 17,538 unmatched, found 27 keys ambiguous and stored 30,224 rows. It dropped 326,308: 316,167 as expansion, 9,399 as operator, 713 as unread and 29 as quoted. A Python mirror of the reader's trace and the core's join reproduced every count. Four findings bear on this thread:

- **Almost everything the Elixir tracer leaves unmatched is outside the project.**
  - 17,444 of the unmatched are calls that no written row names. The largest groups are Module.compile_definition_attributes/6 (5,810), Kernel.defp/2 (3,521), Kernel.to_string/1 from string interpolation (2,407), Kernel.def/2 (1,559), Phoenix.Component.Declarative.__on_definition__/6 (714), Kernel.if/2 (504) and Access.get/2 from bracket access (437).
  - The 94 unmatched module mentions are the project's own. In 23 of them, the written row for an alias names the short form (`config.ex:227`, `Downloadable`). The other 71 are multi-alias braces (`alias Laksa.Content.{...}`), where the tracer names each expanded module at the brace's line.
  - Those 94 are the Elixir population this thread would store.
- **A reference only the toolchain sees can join a written one that shares its line and name**, because rule A's key has no column.
  - Bracket access `x["k"]` traces Access.get/2 with a column and the name `get`, so a line that also writes `Map.get(...)` stores both targets. Laksa has 2 such keys.
  - Interpolation does the same with `to_string` beside a written `X.to_string(...)`: 8 keys for Datespec, 3 for Integer, 2 for Date, 1 for List and 1 for URI.
  - A search answer degrades honestly, with candidates at the syntax level and "one of N" at the door. But `intent search --target Access.get/2` lists exactly those two `Map.get` lines.
  - dc probed a test of whether the text at the traced column spells the name, and no single rule holds. An alias event's column is the `alias` keyword, names ending in `?` or `!` need handling, and multi-alias braces differ.
  - The predicate this thread adds at write has to answer the same question, so it is designed here.
- **A target's place is where the run put it.** The Elixir reader's references carry no definition location, so the core places each target through the index at join time.
  - Consider a file that an incremental compile leaves alone. It keeps the definition line its target had when that file was joined. Meanwhile the target's own file is joined again, and status names no stale path.
  - A Rust run clears this, because every Rust run is full.
  - The roster of defined targets this thread adds is where placement would refresh on every run: a row would read its target's place from the roster instead of carrying it.
- **What the column test costs**, counted over written keys in read files:
  - 30,197 have an event with a column, and join.
  - 8,037 have no event at all. These are typespecs such as `String.t`, and field access such as `.id` and `.assigns`, which the tracer does not report.
  - 6 are dropped because their only events have no column. All six are `is_nil`, most likely rewritten by Ash's `expr`.
  - Separately, the 713 unread events are 696 from `.heex` and 17 from `.eex` templates, which the index holds with no language.
